en: The Section on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
The Chapter on the Propped-Up (Khambhakatavagga), Chapter 30:
The Training Rule on Being Full to the Brim (Samatittikasikkhāpada).
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks received almsfood piled up like a stupa... [as before] ...
"The training is to be observed: 'I shall receive almsfood level to the brim.
Almsfood should be received level to the brim."
Whoever, out of disrespect, accepts almsfood that has been heaped up, commits an offense of wrong-doing.
There is no offense if it was unintentional.
In the case of one who is forgetful,
or one who does not know,
"In the case of one who is insane,
or for one who is a first-time offender.
The tenth training rule is concluded.
